creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`RAD20049` tells you to put a script in a file and `:load` it. `:load` then
rejects that same file with `RAD20049`, so the advice is a loop.

`greet.rad`:

```rad
args:
    name str = "world"

fn do_greet():
    print("hello {name}")
```

```
$ printf ':load greet.rad\ndo_greet()\n' | rad repl
error[RAD20049]: An args block describes a script's interface, which the REPL
has no use for.
  --> <repl>:1:1
```

Nothing in the file runs, so `do_greet` is undefined afterwards too.

`core/error_docs/20049.md` states the behavior it expects: ":load runs the
file's statements against your session ... Its `args` block is skipped, because
there are still no command-line arguments to parse." It isn't skipped -
`replRejectScriptOnlyBlocks` (`core/repl_eval.go`) runs on every turn, loaded
files included. The doc's own worked example is a file with a command block,
which is exactly what `:load` refuses.

Two ways out, pointing in opposite directions:

- Teach `:load` to skip a loaded file's `args`, command and header blocks and
  run the rest. This is what the doc already promises, and it makes `:load`
  useful for the case it exists to serve - pulling your functions into a
  session to poke at them.
- Drop the promise from the doc and from the `= help:`, and say what to do
  instead. Cheaper, but leaves `:load` unable to open most real scripts.

Found during the v0.12.0 docs review, on v0.12.0.
title: REPL :load refuses the files RAD20049 tells you to load
